item.title: Mortgage Rates Drop Slightly to 6.9% APR Today
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: Mortgage Rates Today, Tuesday, November 10: A Little Lower
Mortgage rates dipped slightly today to 6.9% APR for a 30-year fixed-rate loan, down 17 basis points from a week ago. The decline follows a 0.4% rise in October inflation, exceeding economists' 0.3% forecast. The Federal Reserve faces pressure to raise rates again in December and possibly January as inflation remains above its 2% target. While current rates are lower than recent weeks, investors anticipate further hikes, which could push rates higher. Homeowners considering refinancing may benefit if their current rates are 7.4% or higher, though closing costs and loan terms must be evaluated. Lenders adjust rates daily based on market conditions, so locking in a rate is advisable if a favorable deal is secured. Preapproval and budgeting for monthly payments remain critical steps for potential buyers, with tools provided to assess affordability and refinance options.

item.title: Companies Restrict AI Tool Access Amid Rising Costs and Risks
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Bosses are rethinking whether you get access to certain AI tools
Companies are restricting access to advanced AI tools as they shift from broad adoption to cost control and security. Goldman Sachs, Cisco, and JPMorgan are implementing budgets, usage tracking, and employee restrictions. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said advanced models are unnecessary for most tasks, while Cisco’s Jeetu Patel described early AI adoption as akin to learning to ride a bicycle, with later budget limits. JPMorgan capped engineer use of Claude Code at $2,000 monthly. Rising AI spending, now over $177 billion globally, has prompted tighter oversight. A Gartner survey found only 13% of tech executives saw significant AI value. Security risks include 44% of workers using AI improperly and 46% sharing sensitive data. Rippling set monthly AI caps after projecting token costs could reach 40% of its R&D budget, later reduced to 10-15% through efficiency measures. Matt MacInnis of Rippling said cost growth is acceptable if productive.

item.title: San Diego Tourism Projects 34 Million Visitors, $16 Billion Boost
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: San Diego tourism rebounds with a projected 34 million visitors and a $16 billion economic boost this year
San Diego Tourism Authority projects 34 million visitors and a $16 billion economic boost this year. The figure exceeds last year's 32.4 million visitors but remains below pre-pandemic levels. Chief Operating Officer Kerri Kapich attributed last year's flat numbers to economic challenges and post-pandemic recovery. She emphasized tourism's role in the local economy, noting 1 in 8 jobs are tied to the sector. The rebound includes major events like NASCAR and Comic-Con, along with initiatives such as free kids admission in October. A new campaign, 'Eternal Optimist,' aims to attract visitors. Officials also anticipate increased foot traffic from upcoming events like the TED Talk. Kapich highlighted how tourism spending benefits small businesses and tax revenues. The authority is expanding programs to sustain visitor interest year-round.

item.title: Frontier Airlines adds first-class seating, extra-legroom options
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune
Frontier Airlines is introducing first-class and extra-legroom seating options starting March 5. First-class seats, available for $129 one-way, feature a two-by-two layout with 37 inches of pitch. Extra-legroom seats in rows three through eight offer 34 inches of pitch for $90 one-way. The upgrades include USB-C power outlets in first eight rows, set to install by 2027, and Starlink Wi-Fi rollout beginning next year. Bobby Schroeter, chief marketing officer, stated the changes aim to enhance comfort and convenience while maintaining low fares. Passengers can reserve seats online at FlyFrontier.com. The Premium bundle includes a seat, carry-on bag, and priority boarding, while the First bundle adds two checked bags. UpFront Plus seats guarantee empty middle seats in select rows.

item.title: CPCB Explains Delhi Pollution Data Gap During Diwali
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: India: CPCB addresses stark Delhi pollution data gap on Diwali night
India's Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) clarified that a data gap in Delhi's air quality monitoring during Diwali was due to methodological differences, not underreporting. Official data showed an AQI of 400 on Diwali night, while private platforms recorded over 2,000. The CPCB stated its analyzers, calibrated to measure particulate matter up to 1,000 micrograms per cubic meter, treat readings beyond this range as invalid. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee later released data showing PM2.5 levels reached 3,744 micrograms per cubic meter in one area, 60 times the national average, but these were excluded from AQI calculations. The CPCB acknowledged the gap during extreme events like Diwali fireworks and is reviewing its methodology, considering advancements in technology and international practices. The body emphasized that hourly readings outside the calibrated range do not contribute to the 24-hour average. Other reports noted a train derailment in Assam injuring four and an Air India flight isolated at Kolkata airport after a hijack alert.

item.title: Escitalopram Shows Best Relapse Prevention in Antidepressant Study
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Antidepressant escitalopram more effective at preventing relapse, analysis finds
Escitalopram showed the best ability to prevent depression relapse in a study of nearly 10,000 patients, according to an analysis published in The Lancet Psychiatry. The drug outperformed others like agomelatine and duloxetine, while Prozac ranked lower. Researchers emphasized that while escitalopram may be more effective for long-term stability, individual factors like side effects and treatment history should guide decisions. Experts warned against switching medications without consulting a doctor, noting differences in effectiveness were modest. The study compared over a dozen antidepressants, but longer research is needed. Escitalopram, an SSRI, works by increasing serotonin levels. Side effects include sleep issues and weight gain. The NHS and mental health charity Mind advise patients to discuss treatment options with doctors, as what works can vary. Mind highlighted the need for clear information on benefits and side effects, noting many may need to try multiple medications.

item.title: CFTC weighs charges against Kalshi over product notification lapses
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Wall Street regulator poised to bring charges against prediction market giant Kalshi
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is considering charges against prediction market platform Kalshi over alleged failure to notify regulators about new products. A source with direct knowledge of the probe confirmed the CFTC is investigating whether Kalshi improperly bypassed notification requirements for dozens of contracts. Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana called the CFTC's warning a 'procedural error' involving a 'handful of contracts,' many not yet live. The CFTC has not commented on the matter. The agency's scrutiny comes as Democrats prepare to intensify oversight of prediction markets, with Kalshi and Polymarket both under investigation. The CFTC is also examining Polymarket's compliance with a 2022 settlement requiring it to restrict U.S. access. Critics, including CME Group CEO Terry Duffy, have raised concerns about manipulation risks from rapid product launches via self-certification. The CFTC recently warned against overly broad language in product certifications, signaling growing regulatory caution.

item.title: Jimmy Carter's family farm to be preserved and opened to the public
item.description:
Source: ABC News: Top Stories
The Conservation Fund acquired Jimmy Carter's family farm, a 2,458-acre property near Plains, Georgia, to preserve it for public use. The farm, where Carter spent his childhood and returned throughout his life, will open to hunting, fishing, and recreation by next year. The land will transfer to the Georgia Department of Natural Resources the following year. The purchase price was $8.5 million. Carter's final wishes included replanting much of the property with young longleaf pines, expanding the Lanahassee Creek Wildlife Management Area to nearly 7,000 acres. Jason Carter, a grandson, called the land 'home' and praised the conservation effort. Stacy Funderburke of The Conservation Fund noted the farm shaped Carter's legacy and emphasized its role as wildlife habitat. The site is also part of Jimmy Carter National Historical Park, which includes his boyhood home. Carter died in 2024 at 100, and his wife Rosalynn died in 2023.

item.title: L.A. County Fire Reignites After Being Thought Controlled
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Fire at massive L.A. County business triggers air quality alert
A fire at a 15,000-square-foot flooring business in L.A. County reignited Tuesday after being thought controlled. The blaze, which started Monday around 1 a.m. near South Alameda and East 55th streets, took over 200 firefighters four hours to suppress. Firefighters reported pockets of fire remaining in the structure, which housed hardwood planking, cork, and flammable flooring materials. The fire flared again at 4:30 a.m., prompting crews to treat it as a new incident. Lyndsey Lantz, an LAFD spokesperson, noted the fire’s resurgence may have been due to oxygen exposure from damaged walls and materials. While flames did not spread to neighboring buildings, 100 firefighters remained on-site, using aerial units to spray water. The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power shut down power lines near the scene. Manhattan Beach issued an unhealthy air quality alert due to smoke, advising vulnerable residents to limit outdoor exposure. No injuries were reported. Cleanup is expected to take days due to the volume of materials involved.

item.title: SDG&E seeks 8.6% rate hike amid decade-long price surge
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: How SDG&E rates have doubled in a decade
San Diego Gas & Electric seeks an 8.6% rate hike, facing public opposition. Over the past decade, rates have risen 98%, with average monthly electric bills reaching $140. The California Public Utilities Commission typically approves most of SDG&E's requested increases, though not always fully. In 2016, the CPUC approved $1.8 billion in revenue requirements, less than the $1.89 billion requested. SDG&E cites wildfire prevention and grid upgrades as reasons for the current request, echoing arguments from September. Anthony Wagner, SDG&E’s spokesperson, emphasized the company’s commitment to grid resilience. New legislation, including AB 2666, now scrutinizes cost forecasts to prevent overcharging. While approval is likely, SDG&E may not secure all requested funds. The CPUC’s 18-month review process will determine the final rate increase.

item.title: Young Real Estate Professionals Lead 2026 Industry Shifts
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Meet the 2026 rising stars of real estate
Young real estate professionals are reshaping the industry amid challenges like lawsuits over agent commissions, changing tax rules, and AI adoption. Selin Sonmez, cofounder of sublet startup Snag, argues real estate must adapt to a new economic reality. Business Insider highlights 20 under-35 professionals driving innovation, including Joey Ben-Zvi, who closed $200M in deals through his firm. Kenny Burgos, CEO of the New York Apartment Association, advocates for policies balancing rent stabilization and housing supply. Julia Callahan, a real estate PR executive, worked on transforming subway newsstands into retail spaces. Saharsh Chordia developed AI-driven revenue tools at Cortland, emphasizing data-driven real estate. Michael Dillon manages a $3.1B portfolio at Prime Finance and mentors young professionals. Alex Dobosh, an associate director at HKS Real Estate Advisors, executed over $2B in transactions. Tim Donovan, managing director at Midloch, built a $1B firm through relationship-focused strategies. Paige Engeldrum, executive director at Cushman & Wakefield, advises high-profile clients on both sides of real estate deals. These leaders exemplify how the next generation is navigating and transforming the industry.

item.title: IRS adjusts 2027 tax deductions and credits for inflation
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: IRS raises 2027 standard deduction and child tax credit in its annual inflation adjustments
The IRS announced inflation-adjusted tax changes for 2027, effective for 2028 tax returns. Standard deductions rise 3.2%: single filers to $16,600, married couples filing jointly to $33,200, and heads of household to $24,925. The child tax credit increases by $100 to $2,300 per child, with the refundable portion rising to $1,800. The earned income tax credit for workers with no children rises to $685, and for families with two children to $7,552. These adjustments reflect the 2025 law’s inflation-linked provisions. However, several 2025 law benefits, like the $25,000 tip income deduction and $12,500 overtime pay deduction, remain fixed and will expire after 2028 unless extended. The estate tax exclusion increases to $15.48 million, while the top income tax rate stays at 37%, applying to income above $661,375 for singles and $793,650 for married couples. Taxpayers with stable incomes will see reduced tax bills due to inflation adjustments.

item.title: Air France Flight Near Collision at LAX, FAA Reports
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Two planes nearly collide at LAX after Air France flight veers into another aircraft's path, FAA says
Air France Flight 28 made an unauthorized turn at Los Angeles International Airport on Saturday, nearly colliding with an American Airlines flight. The FAA reported the incident, stating the French aircraft veered into the takeoff path of the American Airlines plane bound for Dallas-Fort Worth. Air traffic control issued immediate corrective instructions, and the planes were within 500 vertical feet of each other, approximately a mile apart. Controllers questioned the Air France pilot about instruction clarity. The near miss follows previous LAX safety incidents, including a runway collision on Oct. 6 and a Southwest Airlines emergency landing in November. Air France and American Airlines did not immediately comment on the event.

item.title: College Students Rush to Job Fairs Amid Tight Market
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: College students are lining up at 4:30 a.m. and sprinting for a shot at a job
College students are rushing to job fairs amid a tight market. At the Society of Women Engineers conference in Boston, attendees lined up at 4:30 a.m. for limited booth access, with 14,000 participants, 40% students. Jennifer Scott, SWE’s chief growth officer, noted the event’s packed turnout and shift in hiring practices. With 42.5% of recent graduates underemployed, students like Isabella Wong and Isabel Amaya compete fiercely for internships and entry-level roles. Wong observed that most attendees sought internships, as entry-level jobs remain scarce. Amaya, who secured an offer, highlighted peers landing roles at Bank of America and Bloomberg. However, challenges persist: Allan Morales, a chemical engineering student, found recruiters focused on juniors, while others like Morales’ friend secured offers through pre-conference interviews. Students like Jocelyne Suerte strategize by targeting specific companies, securing offers from multiple fairs. The scramble reflects a broader trend of students prioritizing networking and early opportunities in a competitive job market.

item.title: Nvidia hires Wachtell to investigate Jensen Huang's foreign intelligence ties
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: What we know about Joon H. Kim and Wachtell, the law firm probing Jensen Huang
Nvidia's board has hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of foreign intelligence ties. The probe follows Huang's admission of an extramarital affair and scrutiny over his relationship with Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy. The board announced the independent investigation to determine if Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Wachtell, a corporate law firm with a history of handling high-stakes cases, is led by former Manhattan federal prosecutor Joon H. Kim, who joined the firm as a partner in September. Kim previously served as acting U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York and co-led an investigation into New York Governor Andrew Cuomo's sexual harassment allegations. The firm has also handled cases like Twitter's lawsuit against Elon Musk and NBA investigations into workplace misconduct and salary cap violations. Wachtell's expertise includes corporate governance, mergers, and crisis management, with a focus on internal investigations and regulatory defense.

item.title: Driver Killed, Three Passengers Injured in SR-67 Collision Near Lakeside
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego, San Diego Union-Tribune
A 60-year-old man died and three passengers were injured in a two-vehicle crash on southbound SR-67 near Lakeside on Tuesday. The collision occurred at 8:54 a.m. when a 2015 Toyota Prius turned left onto SR-67, striking a 1998 Dodge Ram traveling southbound. The Prius driver, identified as male, died at the scene. Three occupants—包括 a 39-year-old woman and two male juveniles—were hospitalized with injuries ranging from minor to major. The Ram’s 74-year-old driver, described as unhurt, was not hospitalized. Southbound lanes were closed for about 90 minutes before reopening by 11 a.m. The crash occurred near San Vicente Reservoir in Eucalyptus Hills, north of Lakeside. The cause remains under investigation, with CHP Officer Jasmine Lopez stating drugs and/or alcohol are not factors. The Prius driver’s name was withheld pending family notification. Details about the exact intersection varied slightly between reports.
item.source: ABC 10News San Diego, San Diego Union-Tribune

item.title: U.S. Inflation Remains High, Fed Considers Rate Hikes
item.description:
Source: NYT > Business Original headline: Here’s the latest.
U.S. inflation remained elevated in October, with overall prices rising 0.4 percent and core prices up 0.3 percent, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Energy and food prices drove much of the increase, with food costs rising 0.5 percent and energy prices up 0.7 percent. The Fed faces pressure to raise rates again, as inflation exceeds its 2 percent target. Fed Governor Christopher J. Waller warned that a 25-basis-point rate hike could risk the central bank’s credibility if core inflation remains above 0.3 percent. Two-year Treasury yields rose to 4.67 percent as investors anticipated further rate hikes. While the labor market remains strong, households face financial strain, with mortgage debt hitting $13.4 trillion and HELOC balances rising for the 18th consecutive quarter. Lower-income renters and borrowers are particularly stretched, though student loan delinquencies have eased. The BLS’s October CPI data was adjusted due to missing figures from last year’s shutdown, potentially inflating the year-over-year inflation rate. Economists warn inflation shows no signs of slowing, prompting calls for more aggressive Fed action.

item.title: Aspen Fire Tests AI-Driven Drones for Wildfire Suppression
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Technology Original headline: Testing the new generation of AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones
Aspen Fire Protection District is testing AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones developed by California-based Seneca. The drones, resembling large bugs with four arms and propellers, operate in swarms and can carry 500 to 1,000 gallons of fire foam. Deputy Chief Andy Fisher described them as easy to operate, noting his 12-year-old could fly them. The drones use AI to calculate distance and wind speed, releasing water or retardant at precise angles to suppress flames. Seneca founder Stuart Landesberg claimed the drones can bypass treacherous terrain and have a 5- to 10-mile range. Aspen Fire plans to launch the program by next year, becoming the first department to operate them independently. While proponents like Fisher and firefighter Joe Stutler praise their potential to reduce risk and cost, Stutler remains skeptical about real-world effectiveness, citing lack of data from actual wildfires. The FAA granted a waiver for testing, but drones cannot fly over populated areas and require constant human oversight. Aspen Fire hopes to expand use if the technology proves effective.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Thanksgiving Hosting Tips: Recipes, Decor, and Stress-Reduction Strategies
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: News Original headline: Your guide to hosting a flavorful, cozy and stress-free Thanksgiving
Thanksgiving hosting tips include recipes, decor advice, and stress-reduction strategies. Recipes feature an easier roast turkey with pizza stone, salt-and-pepper turkey breast, cheesy stuffing, garlic bread, vegan pot pie, and Korean-inspired roasted vegetables. Hosting tips emphasize 'generous authority' to balance structure and spontaneity, with advice from Priya Parker on engaging guests with 'magical questions' and focusing on key moments. Decor ideas suggest placing holiday centerpieces at entryways, using sensory elements like scents and textures, and arranging supermarket flowers with specific techniques. Contributors include chefs, writers, and designers offering practical guidance for a stress-free, flavorful gathering.

item.title: Bus Collision Injures 57 in South Korea
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: South Korea: Bus hits 32 vehicles near Seoul, dozens injured
A bus collided with 32 vehicles, including passenger cars, a truck, and four buses, in Seongnam, South Korea, during rush hour. Authorities reported 57 injuries, with nine in serious condition. The bus driver, believed to be in his 60s, told investigators his brakes failed and tested negative for alcohol. He was hospitalized after being freed from the vehicle. Firefighters and emergency medical teams responded to the scene, setting up an emergency station. An investigation into the crash's cause is underway. The incident occurred in Seongnam, a city of nearly 900,000 people located south of Seoul. Local media initially reported 48 injuries, six of them serious, but updated figures show higher numbers. No fatalities were reported.

item.title: California Residents Oppose SDG&E's Proposed 8.6% Rate Hike
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: SDG&E customers urge California regulators to reject proposed 8.6% rate hike at public hearings
San Diego Gas & Electric seeks an 8.6% rate hike, facing strong public opposition at California Public Utilities Commission hearings. Over 100 residents in Santee urged regulators to reject the proposal, citing financial strain as monthly bills could rise by $14 for electricity and $8 for gas. San Diego City Councilmember Sean Elo-Rivera criticized SDG&E for ignoring customer concerns, while Environmental Health Coalition executive director Jose Franco Garcia argued families are already struggling with rising rents and groceries. Opponents claim the hike benefits investors more than customers, with one resident stating, 'SDG&E doesn't profit from keeping your lights on, it profits from what it builds.' SDG&E defended the request as necessary for wildfire mitigation and infrastructure upgrades, stating it aims to control costs and maintain reliable service. The CPUC will review public comments before voting on the proposal, with no immediate decision at the hearings.

item.title: US Warns Madagascar Against Military Ties with Russia
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: US warns Madagascar over growing military ties with Russia
The US has warned Madagascar against deepening military ties with Russia, citing risks of instability similar to the Sahel model. Lt Gen John Brennan, deputy head of US Africa Command, highlighted Madagascar's strategic location in the Indian Ocean and warned against replicating the failed partnerships seen in Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. These countries, under military rule, turned to Russia for support against jihadists but faced continued attacks. Russia has expanded cooperation with Madagascar since the 2025 coup, supplying weapons and military instructors. Brennan expressed concerns about security in the Mozambique Channel, where Islamist militants and pirates threaten maritime trade. He urged caution but acknowledged countries' right to partner with whom they choose. Madagascar's president has publicly supported closer ties with Russia, and the两国 signed defense and trade agreements at the recent Russia-Africa summit. The US emphasized the need to prevent the spread of the Sahel model across Africa.

item.title: Data Center Workers Flood RV Parks, Boosting Industry Sales
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Winnebago ho!
Data center workers are filling RV parks across the U.S., boosting sales for dealers and campground operators. In Cedar Rapids, Iowa, Amana RV Park hosts hundreds of workers from Google and QTS, replacing declining tourist traffic. Managers like Jamie Wolter note the shift forces staff to act as landlords, managing rent arrears and space shortages. RV sales have dropped 13.7% year-over-year, but data center workers are helping dealers like ATC RV Center and Clear Creek RVs maintain sales. Workers use per diems to buy affordable travel trailers, often pairing them with campsite stays. In Louisiana, Meta’s data center project has spurred RV demand, with some parks charging $600 monthly rates. Corporate Mobile Housing in Louisiana now serves 1,500 workers, up from 300 before Meta’s 2024 announcement. However, political challenges loom, with states like Texas and Michigan considering moratoriums on new data centers. As projects wind down, parks may face vacancies, with some owners anticipating sales at steep discounts. Managers like Debbie Coffey in Texas and Heather Kleinpeter in Louisiana highlight the industry’s reliance on temporary housing, while warning of future uncertainty.

item.title: AI Cyberattacks Threaten Global Infrastructure, Experts Warn
item.description:
Source: The Atlantic Original headline: Prepare for the AI Apocalypse Like You’d Prepare for a Snowstorm
AI-driven cyberattacks have surged, targeting critical infrastructure and financial systems globally. Recent incidents include a major software flaw affecting 70% of websites, a Binance hack draining billions, and attacks on refrigeration systems in multiple countries. Governments are responding with heightened preparedness: U.S. military bases must remain operational during cyberattacks, Japan declared a cyber emergency, and the UK advises stockpiling water and food. Cybersecurity experts warn that AI lowers hacking costs, making attacks on individuals and small organizations feasible. Recommendations include using strong passwords, enabling two-factor authentication, updating devices, and vigilance against phishing. Some tech leaders, like Peter Thiel and Sam Altman, have taken extreme measures, storing data offline and preparing physical supplies. Experts like Jeffrey Ladish and Edouard Harris suggest offline data storage, emergency kits, and community preparedness. Cyberattacks have already disrupted water utilities and power plants, raising concerns about broader infrastructure collapse. While not all measures are necessary, basic digital hygiene and emergency supplies are advised to mitigate risks from AI-powered threats.

item.title: San Diego residents oppose SDG&E's 8.6% rate hike proposal
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: San Diego residents pack back-to-back CPUC meetings to oppose SDG&E's proposed 8.6% rate increase for 2028
San Diego residents gathered at two public meetings in Santee to oppose SDG&E's proposed 8.6% rate increase for 2028. Over 100 customers testified against the hike, which would add $14 monthly to electricity bills and $8 to natural gas. Bob Larson, a one-legged resident, joked about the proposal but criticized its affordability. Others, like Dre Andre and Barrett Pall, demanded action against corporate greed and called for leadership to prioritize ratepayers. SDG&E claims the funds will cover wildfire mitigation and system upgrades, but critics argue the company already faces a $1 billion annual profit. Jessica Sustaite highlighted the financial strain on families with $1,000 in debt. The California Public Utilities Commission will vote later in 2027, with advocates hoping the public backlash influences the decision. SDG&E stated it aims to control costs and maintain reliable service.
